question: As part of the March 2021 European Pillar of Social Rights Action Plan, the EU set a target of increasing the rate of adult participation in training to 60% by 2030. 1.
Does the Commission have a clear vision of how it aims to meet that target?
What measures have already been taken that are having a significant positive impact on increasing the rate of adult participation in training in the EU?
answer: The target that at least 60% of all adults should participate in training every year is one of the three targets proposed by the Commission in the European Pillar of Social Rights Action Plan and welcomed by the EU leaders at the Porto summit and the European Council. Member States have defined their 2030 national targets in accordance (1). The progress towards the targets is monitored in the European Semester.

The Commission supports Member States to achieve the target first through financial support, in particular the European Social Fund Plus (2) and the Recovery and Resilience Facility (3), as well as other funds and programmes such as Erasmus+ (4), the Just Transition Fund (5) and Digital Europe Programme (6). The Commission estimates that around EUR 65 billion of EU funds are dedicated to supporting skills.

The Commission’s policy initiatives, such as the actions proposed under the European Education Area (7) and in the European Skills Agenda (8), also contribute to achieving the target. For instance, the Council Recommendation on Individual Learning Accounts (9) of June 2022 aims to empower all adults to continuously develop their skills, providing them with motivation, time and funding.
The Pact for Skills (10) includes 20 large-scale partnerships and 2 500 member organisations, which have already upskilled about 3.5 million people.
